figures.caption: Figure 1: MEG2text: from brain–text alignment to word prediction. (a) The encoder and word head learn alignment against fixed T5 embeddings using the corrected training and evaluation pipeline. (b) A class-balanced linear readout learns to rank candidate words from the frozen features. Two adapters map the target event to the memory and start-query inputs of a frozen T5 decoder, whose word scores are fused with the readout scores. Shaded blue modules are trained in the indicated stage; locks identify frozen modules. Signal traces are schematic.

Figure 2: System improvement and word-level ranking behavior. (a) The 16.92-point gain over published MEG-XL; the hatched backbone step includes pretraining, public-data configuration, code repairs and retraining. (b) Candidate nomination rates on pooled test events, sorted independently for each readout, reveal words that similarity scoring never retrieves. (c) Per-class one-versus-rest AUROC compares separation of each word’s events; points above the diagonal favor cross-entropy. (d) Per-class Top-10 hit rates, ordered by training frequency, show recovery of the six zero-hit classes marked in bold. At coincident values, the blue marker lies inside the orange marker. Panels (b)–(d) use archived scores specified in Section 4; Table 9 gives the values and class counts.

Table 4: Diagnosing candidate competition through score corrections and fitted readouts. Six corrections retain the text embeddings as classifier weights; an in-sample reference and two learned readouts complete the comparison. Mean is four-corpus Top-10 balanced accuracy (%). Hit rates average the pooled per-class Top-10 rates separately for the six zero-hit words and the remaining 44. Nomination rates show the minimum and maximum across candidates. Cross-fitted corrections are fitted on half of the test sentences and evaluated on the other half, then averaged over random splits; fitting and selection details appear in Appendix C.

Table 5: Nine alternative readouts on checkpoint A (four-corpus test mean, %). The first seven add a learned term to the frozen scores of the cross-entropy readout; the last two are fitted with a squared loss on other features. ∆ is the difference from the linear readout with the same loss, with its paired 95% interval where per-event scores were saved.
Table 6: All 20 variants: Top-10 balanced accuracy (%) per corpus and four-corpus test mean. The first seven rows are backbones scored by similarity.
Table 7: Training and selection record. Pooled validation is balanced accuracy after combining the four validation corpora; corpus-mean validation is the four-corpus mean.

Table 9: Per-class results on the pooled test set, classes ordered by number of training events. Hit rate: Top-10 hit rate (%). AUROC: one-versus-rest area under the ROC curve of the class’s score. “sim.” is similarity scoring on checkpoint B and “CE” the cross-entropy readout on checkpoint A. The candidate list is lower-cased, so i is the pronoun.
